item.research_question: How do carbon content (5.44–5.50 wt%) and sintering temperature (1410–1500 °C) synergistically regulate the microstructure and mechanical properties of ultrafine-grained WC-10CoNiFe compared to conventional WC-10Co cemented carbides?
item.material_system: WC-10CoNiFe (multi-principal-element binder) and WC-10Co (conventional binder); starting WC powder 0.4 μm, carbon contents 5.44, 5.46, 5.48, 5.50 wt%
item.processing_route: Planetary ball milling at 420 r/min for 60 h; vacuum drying for 24 h; unidirectional pressing; low-pressure sintering under argon (5.0 MPa) at 1410, 1450, and 1500 °C
item.test_conditions: XRD (Cu Kα, 20°–80°, 5 deg/min); SEM/EDS; microhardness (10 kgf load); transverse rupture strength (three-point bending, ISO 3327-2009, span 14.5 mm)
key_findings: WC-10CoNiFe achieved optimal properties at 5.46 wt% C and 1450 °C with flexural strength 2999 MPa and hardness 1765 HV.
WC-10Co achieved optimal properties at 5.48 wt% C and 1410 °C with flexural strength 3598 MPa and hardness 1853 HV.
WC-10CoNiFe exhibited a finer grain size (0.261 µm) compared to WC-10Co (0.294 µm) under optimal conditions.
Carbon content increase from 5.44% to 5.48% reduced average grain size by suppressing WC dissolution in the binder.
Sintering temperature increase from 1410 °C to 1500 °C increased grain size due to accelerated atomic diffusion.
No η-phase or graphite was detected in samples with carbon content between 5.44% and 5.50%.
The (Co-Ni-Fe) solid solution retained an FCC structure with a lattice constant of 2.880 Å.
item.mechanism: The multi-principal-element (Co-Ni-Fe) binder suppresses the dissolution–precipitation process of WC grains, retaining more tungsten in the hard phase and concentrating grain growth inhibitors (Cr, V) at the hard/binder interface, thereby refining grain size; carbon content regulates WC solubility and prevents η-phase formation, while sintering temperature drives atomic diffusion and grain coarsening.
item.limitations: The text states that while WC-10CoNiFe shows excellent grain refinement, its flexural strength (2999 MPa) is lower than WC-10Co (3598 MPa) due to weaker bonding strength between WC and Ni/Fe compared to Co, indicating room for improvement in stress transfer and crack propagation resistance.
item.future_work: Further optimization of alloy composition and preparation process is expected to enhance mechanical properties while maintaining the advantage of grain refinement.
quotes: The finer grain size of the WC-10CoNiFe alloy (0.261 µm), compared to that of WC-10Co (0.294 µm), can be ascribed to the suppression of the dissolution–reprecipitation process by the multi-principal-element alloy binder.

The synergistic solubilization effect of Ni-Fe in the (Co-Ni-Fe) solid solution effectively suppresses the dissolution–precipitation of WC phase, retaining more tungsten atoms within the hard-phase lattice and thereby enhancing WC peak intensity.
The increase in carbon content reduces the solubility of WC in the binder phase and impedes the dissolved–precipitated behavior of the grains within the same sintering duration.
